name: Pancreatic Cancer
overview: Pancreatic cancer starts in the pancreas, an organ behind the stomach that makes digestive juices and insulin. Because early symptoms are vague, it is often found after it has spread, which makes it one of the harder cancers to treat. When caught early, surgery can remove it, and chemotherapy helps at every stage. Researchers are working hard on better tests and treatments, and care teams can do a lot to ease symptoms.
symptoms: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice)
Belly pain that spreads to the back

drugs.name: FOLFIRINOX
drugs.note: A mix of chemo medicines often used for people healthy enough to handle it.

drugs.name: Gemcitabine (Gemzar)
drugs.note: A long-standing mainstay, used alone or in combinations.

drugs.name: Nab-paclitaxel (Abraxane)
drugs.note: Often paired with gemcitabine.

drugs.name: Whipple surgery
drugs.note: Removes the tumor when the cancer is caught early enough.

redFlags: New yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe belly pain, or vomiting that won't stop needs same-day medical care.

name: Leukemia
aka: Cancer of the blood and bone marrow
overview: Leukemia is cancer of the blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. It crowds out healthy blood cells, leading to fatigue, infections, and easy bruising. There are several types — acute kinds come on fast, while chronic kinds grow slowly, sometimes for years. Treatment has improved dramatically: some forms are highly curable, especially in children, and others can be controlled for the long term with a daily pill.

drugs.name: Cytarabine
drugs.note: A backbone chemo medicine for acute leukemia.

drugs.name: Imatinib (Gleevec)
drugs.note: A daily pill that transformed treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia.

drugs.name: Ibrutinib (Imbruvica)
drugs.note: A pill commonly used for chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.note: Often combined with other medicines for certain types.

redFlags: A high fever, bleeding that won't stop, or sudden trouble breathing needs emergency care — call 911 or go to the ER.

name: Lymphoma
overview: Lymphoma is cancer of the lymphatic system — the network of nodes and vessels that helps your body fight infection. The two main families are Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and the first sign is often a painless swollen lymph node in the neck, armpit, or groin. Many lymphomas respond very well to treatment, and Hodgkin lymphoma is one of the most curable cancers, even when found at a later stage.

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.note: A mainstay for most non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

drugs.name: R-CHOP
drugs.note: The standard first treatment for many non-Hodgkin lymphomas.

drugs.name: ABVD
drugs.note: A common first treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma.

drugs.name: Radiation therapy
drugs.note: Targets specific groups of affected lymph nodes.

redFlags: A rapidly growing lump with trouble breathing or swallowing, or a fever with shaking chills, needs emergency care — go to the ER.

name: Bladder Cancer
overview: Bladder cancer starts in the lining of the bladder, and its most common warning sign is blood in the urine. Smoking is the biggest risk factor. The good news: most cases are found early, while the cancer is still in the bladder's inner layer, where it is very treatable and often curable. Because bladder cancer can come back, regular checkups with a urologist are a key part of care.
symptoms: Needing to urinate more often than usual
Feeling a sudden, strong urge to go
Lower back pain on one side

drugs.name: TURBT surgery
drugs.note: Removes bladder tumors through the urethra — no incision needed.

drugs.name: BCG therapy
drugs.note: Placed directly into the bladder to keep early cancer from returning.

drugs.name: Mitomycin
drugs.note: Another medicine placed inside the bladder after tumor removal.

drugs.name: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy
drugs.note: Used when cancer grows into the bladder muscle.

redFlags: Heavy bleeding with clots or being unable to pass urine at all is an emergency — go to the ER.

name: Kidney Cancer
overview: Most kidney cancers are renal cell carcinoma, which starts in the tiny tubes that filter your blood. Many cases today are found early — often by accident on a scan done for something else — and surgery alone frequently cures those. For cancer that has spread, newer immunotherapy and targeted pills have greatly improved the outlook compared with a decade ago, and treatment keeps getting better.
symptoms: A lump or pain in the side or lower back

drugs.name: Kidney surgery (nephrectomy)
drugs.note: Removing part or all of the kidney often cures early kidney cancer.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab (Keytruda)
drugs.note: Helps the immune system find and attack cancer cells.

drugs.name: Cabozantinib (Cabometyx)
drugs.note: A pill that blocks signals tumors use to grow.

drugs.name: Nivolumab (Opdivo)
drugs.note: Another immune-boosting option, sometimes used in combinations.

redFlags: Heavy or persistent blood in the urine, or severe one-sided back pain with fever, needs same-day medical care.

name: Ovarian Cancer
overview: Ovarian cancer begins in the ovaries or fallopian tubes. Its early symptoms — bloating, pelvic pain, feeling full quickly — are easy to mistake for everyday stomach issues, so it is often found at a later stage. Treatment usually combines surgery with chemotherapy, and newer maintenance pills help keep the cancer from coming back. Women with a family history of breast or ovarian cancer should ask their doctor about genetic testing.
symptoms: Needing to urinate urgently or often
Bleeding after menopause or unusual periods

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.note: The backbone chemo medicine for ovarian cancer.

drugs.name: Paclitaxel (Taxol)
drugs.note: Usually given together with carboplatin.

drugs.name: Debulking surgery
drugs.note: Removes as much of the cancer as possible.

drugs.name: Olaparib (Lynparza)
drugs.note: A maintenance pill that helps keep cancer from returning.

redFlags: Severe belly pain with vomiting, a hard swollen abdomen, or trouble breathing needs emergency care — go to the ER.
